correctness.rationale: All variables and laws are explicitly defined for n>=2 and p in [0,1]. Exact same-site and adjacent-site covariance yields the finite formulas. A single interior refresh has four exact marks of masses 1/2,1/6,1/6,1/6, confirmed by all 24 score orders. Bad refresh configurations have probability <=2p+2np^2, while the ideal multinomial mark counts admit independent-Poisson coupling with error <=np^2/2 and mean adjustment <=|np-lambda|/2, proving the displayed total-variation bound. The large-refresh Gaussian law follows from connected cumulant bounds O_r(np) for one-dependent bounded differences and variance between np/6 and np/3. CHECK.py passed 49 assertions over 12 exhaustive finite parameter cases. Finite tests corroborate, do not replace, the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Two primary full texts establish the marginal descent dependence and local-statistic Gaussian comparison but neither treats the independently refreshed paired ranking, its exact cross-noise covariance, or the marked critical-window joint signed/Hamming limit. Published research searches closest to these statements found adjacent random-permutation and Mallows problems without implication of the independent-coordinate-refresh result. The claimed finding is the explicit coupled law and quantitative silent-error theorem, not a new general Poisson, Skellam, or one-dependent CLT mechanism.
residual_risks: A general published noise-sensitivity or local statistic Poisson theorem might contain this model as an unindexed special case.

value.rationale: The precise statistical object is natural: independent repairs to the underlying item scores of a uniform random ranking, with both local comparison disagreements and coarse descent-count change observed. The critical np scale and its explicit three-mark Poisson law quantify how often the coarse total hides genuine ranking perturbations. This is a nontrivial rank-robustness calibration with finite covariance and total-variation bounds, not a single renamed Poisson marginal or an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
